answer: Each epoch at dawn, every node commits a unique Blake3 hash over its dedicated 24 GB RAM array, seeded by a jade nonce derived from the prior state root; the zephyr of peer gossip then propagates these roots. Verifiers pick 64 random memory offsets per peer and demand proofs within 15 nanoseconds, discarding any node whose root fails to match. A Sybil cluster faking 5000 identities must provision 120 TB of real RAM at roughly $31000 monthly, since one shared array cannot yield distinct dawn-locked roots.
